page.layout: One page of running text in a single column, with marginal notes down the right margin. The right edge of the scan cuts the notes off, so they are only partly legible. No running head, catchword or signature is visible.

main_text.p: nus, quod Maro inquit, prolesque biformis, Minotaurus inest, veneris monimenta nefandæ. [illegible, ~6 letters]Hîc postremò quicquid atrum, quicquid horribile usquam est aut fingitur aspicias: [illegible, ~5 letters]& ut breviter dicam, scelerum ac dedecorum sententia, "Pios veteres longè aliter sensisse de Pontifice Romano, ejusq; judiciis [illegible, ~4 letters]Resp. Audi ergo Bernhardum lib. 4. de confid. ad Eugen. [illegible, ~5 letters]Papam cap. 1. Quem dabis mihi de tota maxima urbe, qui te in papam receperit, precio, seu spe precii non interveniente. [illegible, ~4 letters]Hi invisi terra & cœlo, utrique injecere manus: impii in Deum, temerarii in sanctos, seditio-si in invicem. En judicium antiquitatis. [illegible, ~5 letters]Plura notavimus suis locis, & comprimis demonstravimus, quàm graviter à veritate evangelicâ pontifices Romani aberrarint in hunc usque diem. [illegible, ~4 letters]Quâ igitur conscien-tiâ, quaeso, ab illorum auctoritate de-pendebimus? [illegible, ~5 letters]Audiamus ergo Chri-sti Spiritum in Scripturâ loquen-tem: & nihil nobis de-crit.

page.notes: The right margin is cut off by the edge of the scan. Its note lines are only fragments (for example a line near "nullitatem" at the bottom), so each is marked illegible with an approximate letter count and placed at the nearest text line. The first word "nus," is a fragment carried over from the previous page. The opening quotation mark before "Pios" is a typographic mark and could be a reference sign. The word "quaeso" is printed "quaeso" with a ligature-like ç and may need checking.
